title: MCP servers
subtitle: Connect a public MCP server, or let an assistant build one from API docs. Assigned callers use the tools on every model call and through POST /api/v1/mcp.
readOnly: You can view MCP servers. Changing them needs the permission to manage settings.
installOnly: You can connect a company API key and set access inside your company. Changing the server itself needs permission to manage MCP.

empty.title: No MCP servers yet
empty.description: Connect a public MCP server, or build one from API docs. The gateway calls its tools for every model and provider, and credentials never leave the gateway.

builder.title: Build an MCP server
builder.description: A short brief, a reviewed draft, then who may call it.
builder.stepHint: {step, select, brief {Choose a template, say what to build, and paste the API docs.} review {Check the server and decide which tools exist. The action is what a key permission can block.} access {Allow API keys, or another level, and take tools or actions away from each one.} other {}}
builder.modelEmpty: Add an enabled chat model under Models first.
builder.templateHint: A template fills the instruction. Edit it before drafting.
builder.shareHint: Each company connects its own API key. Calls then use that key instead of the server secret.
builder.templateName: {template, select, readonly {Read only} writes {Reads and changes} full {Everything, including deletes} custom {Your own instruction} other {Template}}
builder.templateText: {template, select, readonly {Build only safe read operations from this documentation. Do not create tools that change or delete data. Set every tool action to read.} writes {Build the read and write operations this documentation describes. Do not build deletes or other irreversible calls. Set reads to action read, and creates and updates to action write.} full {Build every operation this documentation describes. Set safe reads to action read, creates and updates to action write, and deletes or irreversible calls to action delete.} other {}}
builder.instructionHint: The assistant keeps the operations you ask for and skips the ones you rule out.
builder.docsHint: Paste an OpenAPI document, a markdown reference, or the endpoints that matter.
builder.endpoint: Allowed callers reach it at POST /api/v1/mcp. Tool and action rules apply there too.
builder.baseHint: The API origin the tools call, for example https://api.example.com/v1.
builder.toolsHint: Turn a tool off to leave it out of the server. Change the action if the draft classified the call wrong.
builder.accessHint: The server stays private until you allow a key, or turn on access for every caller. Each rule can remove tools or whole actions.
builder.noCaller: No API key can call this server yet.
builder.previewEmpty: Add a key, or pick one below, to see the tools it would get.

permissions.title: Permissions for {name}
permissions.description: Roles decide what a caller may do on this server. A role grants tools by their action, and you can allow or block single tools on top of that.
permissions.tabs: {tab, select, roles {Roles} tools {Tools and matrix} other {View}}
permissions.name: Name
permissions.builtinHint: Built-in roles keep their name. You can change what they grant.
permissions.assigned: {count, plural, =0 {Not used in any access rule yet.} one {Used in # access rule.} other {Used in # access rules.}}
permissions.baselineHint: Applies to every tool left on Default. Tools are classified on the Tools and matrix tab.
permissions.allActionsHint: Also grants tools that have no action yet.
permissions.perToolHint: Allow always grants a tool and Block always removes it, whatever its action. Default follows the actions above.
permissions.noTools: This server has no tools yet. Reload it to fetch its tools.
permissions.deleteBlocked: Remove the role from its access rules first.
permissions.toolsHint: Classify each tool as read, write, or delete. Roles and action blocks follow this classification. Select a cell to switch a tool for one role between default, allowed, and blocked.
permissions.suggestions: {count, plural, one {The server labels # tool as read-only, writing, or destructive.} other {The server labels # tools as read-only, writing, or destructive.}} These labels come from the server itself, so they only count once you accept them.

errors.code: {code, select, MCP_URL_INVALID {Enter a valid http or https URL without credentials.} MCP_URL_INSECURE {Use https, or mark the server as internal to allow http.} MCP_URL_BLOCKED {This address is not allowed. Private addresses need the internal switch, and cloud metadata addresses are always blocked.} MCP_UNREACHABLE {The server could not be reached.} MCP_TIMEOUT {The server did not answer in time.} MCP_HTTP_ERROR {The server answered with an HTTP error.} MCP_PROTOCOL_ERROR {The server did not answer like an MCP server.} MCP_RPC_ERROR {The server returned an MCP error.} MCP_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE {The server answer was too large.} MCP_AUTH_FAILED {The server rejected the credentials.} MCP_AUTH_REQUIRED {The server needs a sign-in. Save it and use Sign in on its card.} MCP_AUTH_SCOPE {The token lacks a permission the server needs. Add the scope and sign in again.} MCP_OAUTH_SUGGESTED {The server asks for OAuth. Choose OAuth as authentication.} MCP_OAUTH_DISCOVERY {The authorization server could not be found. If it runs on a private network, mark the server as internal.} MCP_OAUTH_UNSUPPORTED {The authorization server does not support the secure sign-in this gateway needs (authorization code with PKCE).} MCP_OAUTH_CLIENT_REQUIRED {The authorization server does not register clients automatically. Enter a client ID.} MCP_OAUTH_REGISTRATION {The authorization server rejected the client registration.} MCP_OAUTH_TOKEN {The authorization server did not issue a token.} MCP_OAUTH_STATE {The sign-in expired or was started elsewhere. Start it again.} MCP_OAUTH_DENIED {The sign-in was declined.} MCP_OAUTH_APP_URL {Sign-in needs the console on https or localhost. Check NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL.} MCP_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED {The server speaks no MCP version this gateway supports.} MCP_INPUT_REQUIRED {The tool asked for interactive input, which the gateway cannot provide.} other {The server could not be reached.}}

form.title: {mode, select, edit {Edit {name}} other {Add MCP server}}
form.description: The gateway speaks stateless MCP and falls back to sessions or HTTP+SSE for older servers. It lists the tools and runs them when a model calls them.
form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Models see it as part of each tool name.
form.urlHint: The MCP endpoint, for example https://mcp.example.com/mcp.
form.internalHint: Allows http and private network addresses. Cloud metadata addresses stay blocked.

form.grantOption: {grant, select, client_credentials {Client credentials} other {Sign in with a browser}}
form.grantHint: {grant, select, client_credentials {The gateway gets its own token with a client ID and secret. No person signs in.} other {An operator signs in once. Every assigned caller then uses that sign-in, and tokens renew automatically.}}
form.clientIdHint: {grant, select, client_credentials {The client registered with the authorization server.} other {Optional. Leave empty to register the gateway automatically.}}
form.secret: {type, select, bearer {Token} oauth {Client secret} other {Header value}}

form.scopesHint: Optional. Leave empty to request the scopes the server asks for.

form.enabledHint: Disabled servers offer no tools to anyone.
